title: Check never writes to the folder it checks, not even git's index
assertion: Running `swerepo check` leaves every file and folder unchanged (names, sizes, modification times and contents, git's index included): in a git repository whose index is out of date, with all six default components, a file recorded in .swerepo.toml, the pull-request rules (`--base`) and the command line (`--base --ci` on GitHub Actions, with and without `--json`); and in a folder that isn't a git repository. The test confirms each part ran: a finding from each of the six components and the recorded file, the new dependency found by the diff, and both command-line runs finishing with exit code 1, annotations and parsable JSON.

origin.text: Phase 2 behaviour (SWEREPO-SPEC §15: check is read-only). Drafting this test found a real bug: `git diff` rewrote .git/index when it was out of date, even with --no-optional-locks; check now runs that diff on a temporary copy of the index. Strengthened after Gemini's review (P2-F08) and again after SeamSpec's reviewer found the command-line runs weren't checked and three components weren't confirmed. Proposed for the owner to approve.
